comments.body: Hey man :) have been in Switzerland for about three years now. Came for my masters and decided to stay because I fell in love with the country. I can give you my two cents. Just putting things into perspective, people around mid 20s tend to realize that time and energy is limited. Studies can be occupying and work might take a fair share of your time. You can only habe so many people in your close social circle, and swiss people seem to tend to the connections they habe built over years. So naturally, for us moving to another country, this feeling of wanting to meet new people is probably higher than for the locals. That being said, Zurich and especially ETH fosters and environment of cultural exchange and appreciation for different walks of life. And if you find yourself in an environment where this isnt the case, keep looking around because there are many swiss people that really enjoy different perspectives. And I guess in terms of directly approaching someone, either wait for an organic time for a short one on one. Or engage with the group as a whole, present yourself authentic and outgoing. You might get to know the person you fancy in that process, and she gets a glimpse of you. Either way, dont stress too much and focus on the things you enjoy. Do sports, engage in clubs, whatever really. Do the things you enjoy and your positivity will radiate. Take care man, you will figure it out
comments.author: Freddy_Mercurial
